title: The Lantern of Manchester's mill district
premise: In 1842, Rafael Nystrom, a clockmaker's apprentice passing as a man to keep her trade, is summoned to Manchester's observatory to repair the master clock just as the mill district erupts into strikes and reprisals. A sealed letter hidden in the clock's case implicates her adoptive family in a magistrate's scheme to frame strike leaders for arson, and Rafael must choose between the invisibility that has kept her safe and the record that might keep others alive. Racing the victors' historians and the magistrate's hired men, she gathers testimony from mill workers, a disillusioned soldier, and the magistrate's own clerk, hiding the evidence inside the very clock she was hired to fix. In the end she testifies at the inquest under her true name, at devastating cost to her family and trade, but the truth enters the record before it can be rewritten.
about_author: Noor Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing industrial-era court records in northern England. She writes historical fiction about the people history filed under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Parts
chapters.summary: Rafael Nystrom, disguised as a young man, repairs a merchant's watch in her family's cramped workshop while her father warns her to stay invisible as mill tensions rise. Her POV establishes her precision, her secret, and the fragile peace of survival. Beat: uneasy calm before the summons.

chapters.title: Summons to the Observatory
chapters.summary: A constable delivers an official order: the observatory's master clock is failing and Rafael is named specifically—someone knows her work. She travels through the smoky, restive mill district, observing pickets and soldiers. Beat: pride tangled with dread at being noticed at all.

chapters.title: The Heart That Keeps Time
chapters.summary: Inside the observatory, Rafael meets Keeper Aldous Wren, who guards more than instruments, and discovers the master clock's escapement has been deliberately tampered with. Someone wanted time itself to lie. Beat: first inkling that her craft has been conscripted into something larger.

chapters.title: What the Case Conceals
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV: dismantling the clock's case, she finds a sealed letter naming her family among conspirators in a plot to burn Hartley's Mill and blame strike leaders. She pockets it, heart hammering. Beat: the safe world of small parts collapses.

chapters.title: The Family at the Table
chapters.summary: Home, Rafael confronts her father, who admits he once carried messages for magistrate Corvan before understanding what they were. Her sister Marta begs her to burn the letter. Beat: loyalty versus conscience at the dinner table.

chapters.title: Corvan's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Magistrate Corvan receives Rafael with unsettling warmth, praising her work and hinting he knows what she is—both clockmaker and woman. He offers protection in exchange for silence. Beat: power's velvet glove, and the first real taste of fear.

chapters.title: The Soldier Who Wouldn't Forget
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV: seeking the mill's night watchman, she instead finds Sergeant Elias Brand, a discharged soldier haunted by orders he obeyed at a previous 'accident.' He hints at a pattern of staged fires. Beat: a reluctant ally, and hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Hartley's Mill burns in the night. From a rooftop, Rafael watches the fire she knows was planned, unable to intervene. Marta's POV alternates, showing her terror for Rafael and shame at the family's old complicity. Beat: grief and guilt arrive together.

chapters.title: Names on a List
chapters.summary: Four strike leaders are arrested for arson. Rafael reads the charges and recognizes the letter's language verbatim—the frame was drafted before the fire. Beat: cold clarity; this is machinery, and she knows machinery.

chapters.title: The Clerk in the Corridor
chapters.summary: Corvan's clerk, Thomas Ibbetson, secretly approaches Rafael: he copied the original orders and wants them on the record but fears for his family. Rafael must decide if she can trust a man who served the plot. Beat: fragile trust across enemy lines.

chapters.title: A Clockmaker's Testimony
chapters.summary: Rafael visits the accused weaver's wife, taking a formal deposition in her best hand, learning to be a recorder as well as a repairer. Beat: transformation—from hiding in the record to making it.

chapters.title: What Wren Knew
chapters.summary: Keeper Wren reveals the observatory has long served as a quiet archive of magistrate excess; the clock's tampering was Corvan's test of loyalty. He offers the observatory as sanctuary for evidence. Beat: an unexpected sanctuary, and an old man's penance.

chapters.title: The Search
chapters.summary: Corvan's men raid the Nystrom workshop seeking the letter. Marta lies brilliantly; the family pays in terror and a broken door. Rafael's POV: watching from the street, she understands her invisibility is over. Beat: the price begins to come due.

chapters.title: Ibbetson's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ibbetson hands over copied orders but demands passage for his family before the inquest. Negotiating with Brand, Rafael arranges it—then discovers Corvan has set a trap, watching the clerk. Beat: the plan's first fracture.

chapters.title: The Escape at Canal Bridge
chapters.summary: A night extraction of Ibbetson's family goes wrong; Brand is wounded covering their retreat. Rafael's POV: she carries the man who carries the truth, measuring everything in what can be carried. Beat: sacrifice, and the cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Hidden in Plain Time
chapters.summary: With the inquest days away, Rafael hides the depositions and orders inside the master clock's double case—only she can open it without evidence of entry. Wren's POV: he watches her work and sees the observatory's purpose fulfilled. Beat: the truth, wound and set.

chapters.title: Corvan's Offer, Final
chapters.summary: Corvan corners Rafael: testify to nothing and her family prospers; testify and they are ruined with her. He reveals he has known her secret for years and has kept it as a leash. Beat: the full weight of power's corruption, offered gently.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Inquest
chapters.summary: Rafael and Marta reconcile over the family's history of survival; her father finally blesses her choice, saying he was a courier and she must be a witness. Beat: quiet courage, family remade around truth rather than safety.

chapters.title: The Inquest
chapters.summary: Rafael takes the stand under her full name, Rafael Nystrom, woman and clockmaker, presenting the depositions; Ibbetson's copies corroborate. Corvan's counsel attacks her identity; she refuses to flinch. Beat: climax—truth spoken into the record at last.

chapters.title: The Mechanism Breaks
chapters.summary: The inquest erupts: Corvan attempts to seize the 'forged' clock evidence, but Wren opens the case publicly and the master clock itself, repaired, strikes the hour mid-hearing—a theatrical vindication. The accused are released; Corvan is suspended pending inquiry. Beat: victory, but shaken and costly.

chapters.title: What the Victors Write
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Rafael reads the first newspaper accounts already softening the story—and finds her deposition quoted accurately because it was sworn, on the record, in time. She and Brand begin copying testimony for a private archive. Beat: sober triumph; records outlast headlines.

chapters.title: The Lantern in the Workshop
chapters.summary: Rafael reopens the workshop under her own name, taking apprentices—including girls—while the master clock at the observatory keeps honest time above the district. Final image: her lantern in the window, a small light that outlasts the dark. Beat: resolution—identity claimed, survival redefined.
